subject: Emotions
title: Smell and Attraction
description: A micro-lesson that makes Smell and Attraction usable.

hook.text: Women sniffed sweaty T-shirts and preferred men whose immune systems differed most from theirs. Love starts in the nose.

buildup.text: Claus Wedekind's 'sweaty T-shirt' study showed that MHC gene diversity drives scent preference—unconsciously.

discovery.text: Choosing partners with different immune genes yields healthier offspring. The nose scouts for genetic compatibility.

twist.text: Hormonal birth control reverses this. Women on the pill may prefer similar MHC—and lose attraction when they stop.

climax.text: This may explain post-wedding attraction changes. When birth control stops, scent preference shifts—chemistry follows.

punchline.text: You don't just fall in love with a person. You fall for their immune system.

quiz.question: What did the sweaty T-shirt study reveal about attraction?
options: People prefer different immune system genetics
